newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks end 1.2pct up on expected rate cuts.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks end 1.2pct up on expected rate cuts.

text.p: Greek equities ended 1.20 percent higher on Thursday and brokers said the rise was due to expectations of lower interest rates and expected consolidation in the short-term.

"The market showed consolidation signs on Thursday. It will continue to trade within the 1,250 and 1,300 level in the short-term. But, it is not likely to fall below 1,250 points," said broker Spyros Kotzambasis, at Alki Securities.
The Bank of Greece has announced major changes in its money market operations. It will institute regular weekly repo and depo volume or interest rate tenders to influence short-term rates.
"The bank's attempt to absorb excess liquidity in the market is in line with the government's anti-inflationary policy and this has a positive impact on the bourse," said Kotzambasis.
Standard & Poor's affirmed the Hellenic Republic's BBB-minus long-term foreign currency rating and revised the foreign currency rating outlook to positive from stable, on Wednesday.
Kotzambasis said this was another positive development for the Greek stock exchange.

"Recent international valuations for the Greek bourse have put its P/E ratio as one of the smallest for emerging markets. The market expects more foreign institutional investors to enter soon which is in for a rise in April," he added.

The Athens general share index settled 1.20 percent or 15.37 points higher at 1,295.37 points from Wednesday's 1,280.00 close after opening at 1285.85. Turnover was higher at 12.6 billion drachmas on volume of 3.8 million shares.
Advancers led decliners 154 to 63, with 26 issues unchanged on 243 traded.
Construction shares led the advance, closing 4.42 percent higher. Banking stocks rose 1.65 percent. Investment shares gained 0.92 percent and small caps ended up 0.11 percent.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted lower at 981.00-1019.00. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, closed down 15 drachmas at 5,750.

The recently launched ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $44.24-$45.93. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The recently issued ING Baring Financial Products American- style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted lower at 1,441-1,617 drachmas.
The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998. --Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
